title: feat: Make the examples interactive in the documentation site
body: ## :bookmark_tabs: Summary Ctrl/Cmd + Enter and a run button is added. ## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions The feature was first implemented in https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/pull/5330 by @nalgeon. This is a simplified version without introducing additional dependencies. ### :clipboard: Tasks Make sure you - [x] :book: have read the [contribution guidelines](https://mermaid.js.org/community/contributing.html) - [ ] :computer: have added necessary unit/e2e tests. - [ ] :notebook: have added documentation. Make sure [`MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION`](https://mermaid.js.org/community/contributing.html#update-documentation) is used for all new features. - [x] :bookmark: targeted `master` branch
author: sidharthv96

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body: **question(blocking)**: What does CTRL + Enter do? I've tried it, it doesn't seem to do anything. --- **suggestion(non-blocking)**: Use [``](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/kbd) to describe keyboard keys: ```suggestion {{ ctrlSymbol }} + Enter| ``` Visually, the only difference is that `` elements are monospaced: ### Before ![image](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/assets/19716675/9fd33e77-38ad-4c7e-87c4-a133cbfcc976) ### After ![image](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/assets/19716675/a82791c1-d6fe-408d-9591-070bae5c0edb)

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: > question(blocking): What does CTRL + Enter do? I've tried it, it doesn't seem to do anything. I thought meta would handle both command and control. Will add a separate handler for control then. It's supposed to render the diagram. --- > suggestion(non-blocking): Use [](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/kbd) to describe keyboard keys: I had `` initially, but it was making the meta character smaller. Instead of adding extra CSS, decided to remove kbd as the one without it looked good enough. --- > IMO, we could even completely remove the ```mermaid-nocode blocks if you want. I think @nirname added them explicitly to remove the code, let's not change that behaviour. Let me see how hard it'll be to not break it.
